title: Canonical ell-power reduction adjunction and reconstruction maps
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the completed coefficient ring $A$, normalized coefficient-tower abelian interface $D$, and the actual reduction construction $R$ of [det-sp-reduction-tower-normalized]. Let $r$ be its reduction transported along the coefficient-ring isomorphism to $D(A)$, and let $L$ be exact completed scalar forgetting followed by total right-derived inverse limit [lem-sp-completed-tower-roos]. There exists an adjunction $r\dashv L$ whose unit is invertible at every derived-complete object [def-weil-derived-complete] and whose counit is invertible at every normalized tower [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. No boundedness, constructibility or Tor bound is assumed.

source.place: Adjunction, Unit, Counit and Restriction paragraphs; Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 3.5.7

proof.text: Write ell as a unit times a positive power pi^e. Identify the ell-power strict system with the arithmetic subsequence of the uniformizer system, with its quotient maps and completed projections.

Compose the exact floor-index right-extension Hom bijection with the uniformizer reduction/limit adjunction. Projection-preserving arithmetic cofinality identifies its right adjoint with L. The left-derived universal property and the local tensor-generator formula of R identify its left adjoint with r.

Ceiling-index arithmetic interpolation of a normalized tower gives an effective uniformizer tower; the selected projection adjuncts are its actual counit components. Jointly conservative derived evaluations make the counit invertible.

The actual uniformizer unit is invertible on complete objects. The cofinality comparison respects quotient cone units, so the transported ell-power adjunction has invertible unit on the same complete objects.
